## Louvain clustering

### Some libraries are needed...

```{r}
library(broom)
```

### Analysis

Principal component analysis (PCA) could not be computed with the dataset `matrix_data_filtered`. A subset of 3000 genes will be sliced from the original dataset to perform PCA.

```{r}
random_genes <- sample(1:nrow(matrix_data_filtered), 3000)

random_barcodes <- sample(1:ncol(matrix_data_filtered), 3000)

subset <- matrix_data_filtered[random_genes, random_barcodes]
```

The purpose of this clustering method is classifying different cell types. To do so, first step is doing the PCA for the data.

```{r}
pca_fit <- subset |> 
  select(where(is.numeric)) |>
  prcomp(scale = TRUE)
```

Once `pca_fit` is computed, the data is plotted onto the two principal components.

```{r}
pca_fit |>
  augment(subset) |> # add original dataset back in
  ggplot(aes(.fittedPC1, .fittedPC2)) + 
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(malignant = "#D55E00", benign = "#0072B2")
  )
```
